entries.title: Basic Hematologic Investigations (CBC, Blood Film, Bone Marrow)

testable_competencies.investigation_interpretation: Interpret a CBC/differential, recognize when peripheral blood film review or bone marrow aspiration/biopsy is indicated, as background for every diagnostic unit later in the chapter.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational investigation methodology, not independently testable; frames the condition-specific units that follow.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 42-1 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with anemia, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... Particular attention should be paid to red cell morphology, identification of common causes in specific patient populations, and risk factors for serious underlying conditions.'

testable_competencies.classification: Classify anemia by MCV (microcytic/normocytic/macrocytic) and reticulocyte-response as the entry point to the specific-diagnosis units below.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose the cause, severity, and complications of anemia in a given patient population.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 42-2 directly names elevated hemoglobin, matching this unit's primary-vs-secondary erythrocytosis diagnostic approach.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate primary (e.g., polycythemia vera) from secondary (hypoxic, EPO-mediated, or spurious) causes of an elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for thrombocytopenia specifically (full-registry search returned zero matches); objective 15-1's bleeding/bruising differential is the nearest adjacent evidence since low platelet count is a leading cause of that presentation, though the objective text does not name thrombocytopenia verbatim.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Generate a differential for thrombocytopenia (decreased production, increased destruction/consumption, sequestration) and recognize features requiring urgent workup (e.g., microangiopathic hemolysis, active bleeding).

entries.title: Thrombocytosis (Approach)

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate reactive (secondary) from clonal (myeloproliferative) causes of an elevated platelet count.

entries.zero_question_reason: Supports interpretation of an elevated platelet count and distinction of reactive from clonal causes, but no canonical MCC objective independently anchors thrombocytosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pancytopenia's anemia component falls under objective 42-1's diagnostic scope, though the objective does not itself address the tri-lineage (WBC/platelet) component.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pancytopenia's leukopenia component, and its overlap with the objective's named 'acute leukemia' and 'febrile neutropenia' emergencies, falls under objective 120's scope, though pancytopenia itself is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Generate a differential for pancytopenia (bone marrow failure/infiltration, peripheral destruction, sequestration) and identify features requiring urgent bone marrow evaluation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 120 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with a white blood cell abnormality, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity and complications... attention should be paid to distinguishing those conditions which are life threatening (overwhelming sepsis, acute leukemia, febrile neutropenia)... from those that are non-urgent.'

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Fever in the immune compromised host / recurrent fever
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Febrile neutropenia (a named emergency under objective 120) is also the paradigmatic presentation covered by objective 107-4's immunocompromised-fever framework, supporting elevated urgency-recognition depth for this component.

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate the causes of neutrophilia, lymphocytosis, eosinophilia, and leukemoid reaction (reactive vs. malignant) and of neutropenia, lymphopenia, and agranulocytosis (production failure vs. peripheral destruction vs. drug-induced).
testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize febrile neutropenia as a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics, distinct from non-urgent WBC abnormalities.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 54 is an exact match: 'Given a patient with lymphadenopathy, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications, and will initiate an appropriate management plan. In particular, the candidate will determine the need for a biopsy.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Localize and characterize lymphadenopathy (generalized vs. localized, size, consistency, tenderness) and determine the need for biopsy vs. observation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for splenomegaly specifically (full-registry search for 'spleen' returned zero matches); objective 2's abdominal-mass diagnostic approach is the nearest adjacent evidence, since an enlarged spleen is examined and worked up as a left-upper-quadrant abdominal mass, though splenomegaly is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Generate a differential for splenomegaly (infectious, congestive, hematologic/infiltrative, hemolytic) and recognize indications for further hematologic workup.

entries.title: Iron Metabolism and Iron Deficiency Anemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Iron deficiency anemia is the paradigmatic microcytic anemia captured by objective 42-1's 'diagnose the cause, severity, complications... particular attention to red cell morphology' requirement, and the objective's own rationale explicitly flags identifying risk factors for serious underlying conditions (e.g., occult GI malignancy) that iron studies/source-of-bleeding workup addresses.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Interpret iron studies (ferritin, TIBC, transferrin saturation) to diagnose iron deficiency and distinguish it from other microcytic anemias.
testable_competencies.workup: Identify the underlying source of iron loss (e.g., occult GI bleeding, menorrhagia, malabsorption) and initiate appropriate investigation by age/risk factors.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Anemia of chronic disease/inflammation is a major microcytic-to-normocytic etiology covered by objective 42-1's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize anemia of chronic disease/inflammation (elevated ferritin, low TIBC, hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration) in a patient with an underlying chronic inflammatory, infectious, or malignant condition and distinguish it from iron deficiency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sideroblastic anemia is a microcytic-anemia etiology (hereditary or acquired) covered by objective 42-1's differential, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sideroblastic anemia (ring sideroblasts on bone marrow, elevated ferritin, high transferrin saturation) and its major causes (hereditary, MDS-associated, alcohol, lead, isoniazid).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 77 requires diagnosing the cause, severity, and complications of poisoning generally and initiating management based on identified cause; lead poisoning is a named toxic exposure fitting this scope, though the objective's retrieved excerpt does not name lead specifically.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Lead poisoning's basophilic-stippling microcytic anemia is a recognized cause under objective 42-1's differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lead poisoning as a cause of microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling and identify exposure risk factors (e.g., old paint, occupational).
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate investigation (blood lead level) and management (remove exposure source, chelation in severe cases).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Normocytic-anemia classification (reticulocyte-based: hemolytic/hemorrhagic vs. hypoproliferative) is a component of objective 42-1's broader classification-by-morphology requirement.

testable_competencies.classification: Use the reticulocyte count to differentiate hypoproliferative normocytic anemia (e.g., early iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, bone marrow failure) from a hyperproliferative response (hemolysis, acute blood loss).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Aplastic anemia is a normocytic anemia etiology under objective 42-1's scope, though its bone-marrow-failure/pancytopenia mechanism is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Aplastic anemia's concurrent leukopenia component touches objective 120's scope only tangentially, since the primary presentation and testable competency is the anemia/pancytopenia picture.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize aplastic anemia (pancytopenia with hypocellular bone marrow) and identify major causes (idiopathic autoimmune, drug/toxin, viral, inherited).
testable_competencies.management: Recognize the need for urgent hematology referral and supportive care (transfusion, infection prophylaxis) pending transplant/immunosuppressive therapy evaluation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hemolytic anemia is a major anemia category under objective 42-1's scope; this unit's intravascular-vs-extravascular classification framework is not itself named in the objective text but is the standard diagnostic-reasoning tool for that category.

testable_competencies.classification: Use hemolysis screening tests (LDH, haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin, reticulocyte count, blood film, Coombs test) to confirm hemolysis and classify it as intravascular vs. extravascular, framing the specific diagnoses in SU-H-17 through SU-H-22.

entries.title: Thalassemia (Alpha and Beta, Minor/Major/Intermedia)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Thalassemia is a classic microcytic anemia distinguished by 'identification of common causes in specific patient populations' (Mediterranean/South/Southeast Asian/African heritage), directly matching objective 42-1's own rationale text.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize thalassemia trait/minor vs. major/intermedia by CBC pattern (low MCV with normal/high RBC count), ethnicity-based pretest probability, and Hb electrophoresis, distinguishing it from iron deficiency anemia.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize the transfusion/chelation-dependence spectrum and genetic counselling indication.

do_not_test: Exact allelic/genotype deletion patterns (e.g., cis vs. trans 2-gene deletion) - specialist-level molecular detail beyond generalist decision value.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for sickle cell disease specifically (full-registry search for 'sickle cell' returned zero matches, a registry-coverage-gap pattern already documented in chapters E, G, GS, GM, GY); sickle cell disease's chronic hemolytic anemia component falls under objective 42-1's scope, and its 'risk factors for serious underlying conditions' rationale supports the vaso-occlusive/aplastic/sequestration crisis content, though SCD is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sickle cell disease genotypes (HbSS, HbSC, HbS-beta-thal) and their chronic manifestations (hemolytic anemia, functional asplenia/infection risk, growth delay).
testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize and initiate management of acute sickle cell crises (vaso-occlusive, aplastic, splenic sequestration, acute chest syndrome) as hematologic emergencies, including indications for exchange transfusion.
testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize preventive measures (vaccination, prophylactic penicillin in children, hydroxyurea) and screening for chronic complications (stroke risk, retinopathy, pulmonary hypertension).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: AIHA is a hemolytic anemia etiology under objective 42-1's scope; not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish warm from cold AIHA using the direct Coombs (direct antiglobulin) test and blood film findings (spherocytes vs. agglutination), and identify primary vs. secondary causes (lymphoproliferative disease, SLE, drugs, infection).

entries.title: Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia / Thrombotic Microangiopathy (Definition and Etiology)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses MAHA/TMA directly; objective 15-1 is the nearest adjacent evidence given the concurrent thrombocytopenia/bleeding-risk overlap, though the objective text does not name MAHA and this unit's own clinical action is delegated to SU-H-26 (TTP/HUS) and SU-H-30 (DIC).

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize schistocytes on blood film as the hallmark of intravascular RBC fragmentation and generate a differential (TTP, HUS, DIC, malignant hypertension, eclampsia/HELLP, mechanical heart valve, disseminated malignancy, drug-induced) that routes to the specific-diagnosis units elsewhere in this chapter.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are hereditary RBC-membrane-defect hemolytic anemias under objective 42-1's scope; neither is named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize hereditary spherocytosis (spherocytes, elevated MCHC, increased osmotic fragility) and hereditary elliptocytosis (elliptocytes) as intrinsic membrane-defect hemolytic anemias, and identify splenectomy as the definitive treatment for severe disease with pre-splenectomy vaccination.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: G6PD deficiency is a hereditary enzymopathy causing hemolytic anemia under objective 42-1's scope; not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Episodic hemolysis in G6PD deficiency is classically drug/oxidant-triggered, loosely analogous to objective 77's exposure-based diagnostic framework, though G6PD deficiency is an endogenous enzymopathy rather than poisoning per se.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize X-linked G6PD deficiency presenting as episodic hemolysis triggered by oxidative stress (drugs, infection, fava beans), with Heinz bodies and bite cells on blood film.
testable_competencies.management: Identify and avoid triggering drugs/exposures; recognize that G6PD assay may be falsely normal during acute hemolysis (high reticulocyte G6PD levels).

entries.title: Macrocytic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Vitamin B12 and folate deficiency are the paradigmatic megaloblastic (macrocytic) anemias under objective 42-1's 'diagnose the cause... particular attention to red cell morphology' requirement.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish B12 from folate deficiency (elevated MMA and homocysteine in B12 deficiency vs. isolated elevated homocysteine in folate deficiency) and identify their major causes (pernicious anemia, malabsorption, dietary, medication-induced).
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize neurologic manifestations specific to B12 (not folate) deficiency and the risk of precipitating/worsening them with unrecognized folate-only replacement.

entries.title: Normal Hemostasis Physiology

testable_competencies.physiology: Recognize the stages of hemostasis (vascular spasm, primary platelet plug, secondary coagulation cascade, fibrinolysis) as background for the bleeding- and clotting-disorder units that follow.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal physiology background, not independently testable; underlies SU-H-25 through SU-H-32.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ITP is a leading cause of isolated thrombocytopenic bleeding/bruising, matching objective 15-1's diagnose-cause-severity-complications scope; a diagnosis of exclusion confirmed by isolated thrombocytopenia with an otherwise normal blood film.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose ITP as a diagnosis of exclusion in a patient with isolated thrombocytopenia and mucocutaneous bleeding, distinguishing primary from secondary (drug-induced, lymphoproliferative, autoimmune-associated) ITP.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize indications for treatment (corticosteroids, IVIG, TPO-receptor agonists, splenectomy) based on bleeding severity and platelet count, and recognize when observation alone is appropriate.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: TTP and HUS are hematologic emergencies with multi-organ ischemic complications matching objective 9-2's urgency-recognition scope, though neither is a classic 'shock' presentation per se and neither is named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: TTP/HUS present with thrombocytopenic bleeding tendency alongside microangiopathic hemolysis, falling under objective 15-1's broader bleeding-disorder scope.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize the pentad/features of TTP (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, +/- neurologic changes, renal dysfunction, fever) and HUS (typically post-diarrheal, renal-predominant) as medical emergencies.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate urgent plasma exchange for suspected TTP without delaying for confirmatory testing, and recognize that platelet transfusion is generally contraindicated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: vWD is the most common inherited bleeding disorder and a leading cause of mucocutaneous bleeding/bruising, directly matching objective 15-1's diagnostic scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize vWD presenting with mucocutaneous bleeding and a prolonged PTT with normal PT, confirmed by vWF antigen/activity and factor VIII level.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize desmopressin (DDAVP) and vWF-containing factor concentrates as management options.

entries.title: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, and Factor XI Deficiency

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hemophilia A/B are classic X-linked bleeding disorders (hemarthroses, deep-tissue bleeding) directly matching objective 15-1's diagnostic scope; Factor XI deficiency shares the identical isolated-prolonged-PTT diagnostic pathway.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the X-linked hemarthrosis/deep-muscle-bleeding pattern of hemophilia A (factor VIII) and B (factor IX), confirmed by isolated prolonged PTT and specific factor assay.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize factor replacement as the mainstay of acute bleed management and prophylaxis.

entries.title: Coagulopathy of Liver Disease and Vitamin K Deficiency

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are acquired multi-factor coagulopathies (decreased hepatic synthesis of vitamin-K-dependent clotting factors) presenting with bleeding, under objective 15-1's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Synthetic-function coagulopathy is a recognized complication assessed under objective 52's abnormal-liver-function-tests scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize elevated PT/INR from decreased hepatic synthesis of factors II, VII, IX, X (liver disease) or from vitamin K deficiency/warfarin effect, and distinguish the two by response to vitamin K administration.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: DIC is a hematologic emergency frequently precipitated by and complicating shock (sepsis, trauma, obstetric catastrophe), matching objective 9-2's urgency-recognition scope though DIC is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: DIC's consumptive-coagulopathy bleeding presentation falls under objective 15-1's scope.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize DIC as concurrent bleeding and thrombosis (elevated D-dimer, low fibrinogen, prolonged PT/PTT, thrombocytopenia, schistocytes) triggered by an underlying critical illness (sepsis, trauma, obstetric emergency, malignancy).
testable_competencies.management: Treat the underlying trigger and provide supportive blood-product replacement (FFP, cryoprecipitate, platelets) guided by bleeding severity.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for thrombophilia specifically; objective 15-2's risk-assessment scope ('take further measures to assess the likelihood of occurrence') is the nearest adjacent evidence for identifying a hereditary or acquired hypercoagulable state.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical features prompting a thrombophilia workup (unprovoked/recurrent VTE, VTE at young age, unusual sites, arterial thrombosis, recurrent miscarriage) and identify the major hereditary (Factor V Leiden, prothrombin gene mutation, protein C/S or antithrombin deficiency) and acquired (antiphospholipid syndrome) causes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for established DVT/PE diagnosis and treatment (full-registry search for 'deep vein', 'pulmonary embolism' returned zero matches); objective 15-2 is the only related evidence found, but its own title and text are scoped to primary prevention/risk-assessment rather than the diagnosis-and-treatment-of-established-VTE content this Toronto Notes unit covers, so mapping strength is capped at MODERATE despite this being one of the chapter's highest-yield topics.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Use pretest probability (e.g., Wells score) combined with D-dimer and imaging (compression ultrasound for DVT, CT pulmonary angiography for PE) to diagnose VTE.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate anticoagulation for confirmed VTE, recognize indications for thrombolysis in massive/submassive PE, and determine anticoagulation duration based on provoked vs. unprovoked status.

entries.title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 120's own rationale text explicitly names 'acute leukemia' as one of the life-threatening WBC-abnormality presentations the candidate must distinguish from non-urgent conditions.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize AML presenting with pancytopenia symptoms (fatigue, infection, bleeding) +/- blasts on peripheral smear as a hematologic emergency requiring urgent hematology referral and bone marrow biopsy.
testable_competencies.complication_recognition: Recognize leukostasis and DIC (particularly in acute promyelocytic leukemia) as life-threatening AML complications.

do_not_test: WHO molecular/cytogenetic subclassification of AML and specific induction chemotherapy regimens - specialist hematopathology/oncology detail beyond generalist decision value.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: MDS presents with cytopenias including WBC-lineage dysplasia under objective 120's broader scope, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize MDS in an older adult with unexplained cytopenia(s) and dysplastic blood film/marrow findings, and recognize its risk of transformation to AML.

entries.title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CML presents with marked leukocytosis under objective 120's broader WBC-abnormality scope, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize CML presenting with marked leukocytosis with a left shift across all maturation stages, splenomegaly, and confirmed by the BCR-ABL/Philadelphia chromosome.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (e.g., imatinib) as first-line treatment.

do_not_test: Specific TKI selection/sequencing and resistance-mutation management - specialist oncology detail.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Polycythemia vera is the primary (clonal, JAK2-mutated) cause of an elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit, the paradigmatic diagnosis under objective 42-2's scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose PV using JAK2 mutation testing and diagnostic criteria, distinguishing it from secondary/spurious erythrocytosis.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize thrombosis as the major PV complication and therapeutic phlebotomy plus low-dose aspirin as first-line management.

entries.title: Myelofibrosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses myelofibrosis directly; the leukoerythroblastic blood film picture touches objective 120's WBC-abnormality scope only tangentially, since myelofibrosis's primary presentation is marrow fibrosis with massive splenomegaly rather than an isolated WBC count abnormality.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize myelofibrosis presenting with massive splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms, and a leukoerythroblastic blood film with teardrop cells.

entries.zero_question_reason: Only WEAK adjacent MCC evidence found; retained as a distinct unit because Toronto Notes gives it independent topic status among the myeloproliferative neoplasms.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses essential thrombocythemia directly; its thrombosis-risk management overlaps objective 15-2's scope only loosely, since the objective's title/text describe venous-thrombosis prevention generally rather than a clonal marrow disorder.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize essential thrombocythemia as a clonal cause of marked thrombocytosis with elevated thrombosis (and paradoxical bleeding) risk, distinguished from reactive thrombocytosis.

entries.title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ALL is an acute leukemia presenting with WBC-lineage abnormality, pancytopenia, and constitutional symptoms, under objective 120's 'acute leukemia' life-threatening-presentation scope, though ALL is not separately named from AML in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize ALL as the most common childhood malignancy, presenting with bone pain, pancytopenia symptoms, and lymphadenopathy/hepatosplenomegaly, and recognize its urgency for hematology-oncology referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Predominantly a pediatric malignancy; may overlap chapter P (Pediatrics, not yet mapped) at a more developmentally-specific level. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

entries.title: Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Lymphoma is the leading malignant cause of pathologic lymphadenopathy and the principal reason objective 54 requires the candidate to 'determine the need for a biopsy.'

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize painless, progressive lymphadenopathy +/- B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) as suggestive of lymphoma and initiate excisional lymph node biopsy.
testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish Hodgkin lymphoma (bimodal age distribution, contiguous spread, Reed-Sternberg cells) from non-Hodgkin lymphoma (broader age range, non-contiguous spread, heterogeneous subtypes) at a recognition level.

do_not_test: Specific NHL molecular subtype classification and chemoimmunotherapy regimen selection - specialist oncology detail beyond generalist decision value.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CLL frequently presents with generalized lymphadenopathy under objective 54's scope, though not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CLL's marked, often incidentally-found lymphocytosis falls under objective 120's WBC-abnormality scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize CLL as the most common adult leukemia in Western countries, often an incidental finding of marked lymphocytosis with smudge cells on blood film in an asymptomatic older adult.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Anemia is a core presenting CRAB-criterion of multiple myeloma, falling under objective 42-1's diagnostic scope, though myeloma is not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Myeloma cast nephropathy/renal failure is a CRAB-criterion complication under objective 89-2's scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize multiple myeloma via the CRAB criteria (hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions) plus M-protein on serum/urine protein electrophoresis and elevated free light chains.
testable_competencies.complication_recognition: Recognize hypercalcemia, renal failure, and pathologic fracture/cord compression as urgent myeloma complications requiring prompt management.

entries.title: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Unknown Significance (MGUS)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses MGUS directly; the only loosely adjacent evidence is objective 42-1, since MGUS is diagnosed by excluding myeloma-associated anemia/CRAB features, but MGUS itself is typically asymptomatic and not an anemia presentation.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish MGUS (asymptomatic M-protein <30 g/L, <10% marrow plasma cells, no CRAB features) from multiple myeloma, and recognize its need for periodic monitoring given progression risk.

entries.zero_question_reason: Only WEAK adjacent MCC evidence found; retained as a distinct unit because distinguishing MGUS from myeloma is itself a recognized generalist competency and Toronto Notes gives it independent topic status.

entries.title: Lymphoplasmacytic Lymphoma (Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia directly; lymphadenopathy is only an occasional feature of this predominantly IgM-hyperviscosity-driven disorder, making objective 54 a loose secondary anchor at best.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia as an IgM-secreting lymphoproliferative disorder presenting with hyperviscosity symptoms, distinguishing it from multiple myeloma (no CRAB/bone lesions).

entries.zero_question_reason: Only WEAK adjacent MCC evidence found; retained as a distinct unit because Toronto Notes gives it independent topic status among the mature B-cell clonal proliferations.

entries.title: Oncologic Emergencies: Hyperviscosity Syndrome and Tumour Lysis Syndrome

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both hyperviscosity syndrome and tumour lysis syndrome are acute, life-threatening complications of hematologic malignancy/its treatment, matching objective 9-2's urgency-recognition scope, though neither is named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize hyperviscosity syndrome (mucosal bleeding, visual changes, neurologic symptoms in a patient with a high M-protein or extreme leukocytosis) and initiate urgent plasmapheresis/leukapheresis.
testable_competencies.emergency_recognition_2: Recognize tumour lysis syndrome (hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia, hypocalcemia, acute kidney injury) as a risk after initiating chemotherapy for a high-burden hematologic malignancy and initiate prophylaxis (hydration, allopurinol/rasburicase) and monitoring.

entries.title: Blood Product Selection and Transfusion Indications

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 121-1's informed-consent requirement directly applies to transfusion, a procedure with known risks requiring specific consent, though transfusion itself is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Platelet and coagulation-factor product selection is a management step for the bleeding disorders objective 15-1 addresses, though transfusion product selection itself is not named.

testable_competencies.product_selection: Select the appropriate blood product (packed RBCs, platelets, FFP, cryoprecipitate) and transfusion threshold for a given clinical scenario (e.g., restrictive vs. liberal RBC transfusion strategy).

entries.title: Acute and Delayed Blood Transfusion Reactions

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute hemolytic and anaphylactic transfusion reactions can present as shock, matching objective 9-2's urgency-recognition scope though transfusion reaction is not named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction is a leading cause of new fever during/after transfusion, under objective 107-1's fever-diagnosis scope.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize and immediately stop the transfusion for suspected acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (fever, flank pain, hemoglobinuria, shock) vs. manage febrile non-hemolytic, allergic, TRALI, or TACO reactions appropriately, and recognize delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction and iron overload as delayed complications.

entries.title: Antiplatelet and Anticoagulant Therapy (Reference)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Anticoagulant selection is the core management step of objective 15-2's thrombosis-prevention scope; antiplatelet therapy is adjacent management for arterial thrombotic risk.

testable_competencies.drug_class_selection: Recognize the general indications, contraindications, and monitoring principles for antiplatelet agents and for anticoagulant classes (vitamin K antagonists, DOACs, heparins) without reference to a specific current dosing regimen.

do_not_test: Specific current dosing regimens, reversal-agent dosing, and drug-interaction detail - encoded during question-generation source research, not at this scope stage, per project accuracy rules on changing treatment recommendations.
